# Campaign Brief: PLG MCP · Tech & Software · AE

## Executive Summary

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Goal** | Drive 200 self-serve connector setups or platform signups from individual-contributor AEs and full-cycle sellers at US tech and software companies under 5,000 employees within 8 weeks. |
| **Primary KPI** | Connector Setups & Platform Signups: 200 |
| **Target Audience** | Individual-contributor Account Executives and full-cycle sellers at US-based tech and software companies under 5,000 employees. These reps own the full revenue motion — sourcing, mapping buying committees, and closing — meaning research time directly competes with selling time. Their core pain: stale territory plans, buying committees mapped one stakeholder too late, and 10–15 minutes of manual hunting before every call. They need faster access to verified B2B contact data without leaving their existing workflow. |
| **Primary Channel** | Email |
| **Core Hook** | Full-cycle sellers pay for pipeline twice — 750M+ contacts inside Claude turn territory research into a question, not an afternoon. |
| **Timeline** | 2025-07-28 to 2025-09-19 |

---

## Goal & Success Metrics

### KPI Dashboard

| Metric | Target | How Measured |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| Connector Setups & Platform Signups | 200 | Unique completed connector setups in Claude or platform signups tracked via landing page conversion event |
| Email Reply Rate | 6% | Positive + neutral replies divided by total emails delivered, tracked per step |
| Step 1 → Step 2 Progression Rate | 40% | Percentage of non-reply recipients from Step 1 who receive and open Step 2, indicating sequence health |
| Landing Page Click-Through Rate | 3% | Clicks on the Step 2 landing page link divided by Step 2 emails delivered |
| Sequence Completion Rate | 70% | Percentage of contacts who receive both steps without unsubscribing, bouncing, or triggering a stop rule |

### Guardrails
- Max daily volume: 250
- Negative reply threshold: 5%

---

## Offer & CTA Spec

| Component | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| **Deliverable** | Instant access to 750M+ B2B contact records (emails, mobile numbers, company details) via graph8's MCP server inside Claude — or directly in the graph8 browser platform with 2,500 credits at signup. One custom connector included. Works on the Claude free plan. |
| **Time-to-Value** | Same session — connect once and search from chat immediately; browser platform is live at signup with 2,500 credits |
| **Primary CTA** | Use the paste-ready territory or committee-mapping prompt to run your first search (Step 2 CTA — one link to sending-domain landing page) |
| **Fallback CTA** | Reply to tell us your biggest research time-sink (Step 1 soft reply CTA — no link) |

---

## Why Now - Trigger Signals

| Signal | Priority | Rationale |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Recently promoted to a new territory or account patch | High | New territory assignments force an immediate rebuild of contact lists, org maps, and account intelligence — exactly the pain graph8 MCP eliminates. These reps are actively hunting for tools to accelerate ramp. |
| Hiring surge or team expansion at the prospect's company | High | Growing companies add new buying committee members and decision-makers rapidly, making committee mapping stale within weeks. Full-cycle AEs at these accounts face compounding research overhead that 750M+ live records directly addresses. |
| Prospect is using or discussing Claude / Anthropic tools on LinkedIn or in public forums | High | Active Claude users are the zero-friction install path for the MCP connector — they can set it up in minutes on the free plan. This signal collapses the adoption barrier from days to a single chat session. |
| Prospect's company recently closed a Series A–C funding round | Medium | Post-funding growth pressure accelerates sales hiring and territory expansion, creating immediate demand for scalable prospecting infrastructure. Full-cycle AEs at funded startups are especially resource-constrained and receptive to self-serve efficiency tools. |
| Prospect is active on LinkedIn with posts or comments about prospecting, pipeline, or research workflows | Medium | Public complaints or questions about research overhead indicate felt pain and openness to solutions — ideal timing to land a message framed around turning that workflow into a question. |
| Company headcount is 50–500 (no dedicated RevOps or SDR support) | Medium | At this size, AEs are almost certainly doing their own prospecting with no tooling backstop. The absence of a dedicated support function makes the self-serve MCP value prop land harder and faster. |

---

## Contact Policy

| Channel | Max/Week | Hours | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|
| Email | 1 | 8am-5pm local (US time zones) | 2-step sequence only. Step 1 is linkless with a soft reply CTA. Step 2 delivers a paste-ready prompt with one link to a sending-domain landing page (never graph8.com). No pricing in any email. Only approved data claim is 750M+ contacts. Minimum 3 business days between Step 1 and Step 2. Send Tuesday–Thursday for best deliverability. List 1002040, email-validated valid-only contacts only. |

### Stop Rules
- Unsubscribe or opt-out request — remove immediately and suppress from all future sends
- Hard bounce — suppress from sequence and flag for list hygiene
- Negative reply (e.g., 'not interested', 'wrong person', 'stop emailing me') — halt sequence, log sentiment, suppress
- Out-of-office reply indicating departure or role change — pause sequence, re-evaluate contact validity
- Conversion event confirmed (connector setup or platform signup) — remove from remaining steps immediately
- Prospect is a Claude Team or Enterprise workspace member flagged as requiring admin approval — add note for follow-up but do not re-sequence without admin confirmation context
- Campaign-level negative reply rate exceeds 5% — pause full campaign and review messaging before resuming

---

## Targeting Constraints

### Geographic Targeting

| Include | Exclude |
|---------|---------|
| United States | Canada |
| - | EMEA |
| - | APAC |
| - | LATAM |

### Industry Targeting

| Include | Exclude |
|---------|---------|
| Technology | Government |
| Software | Defense |
| SaaS | Healthcare / HIPAA-regulated entities |
| Internet | Financial Services (broker-dealer / SEC-regulated) |
| Cloud Infrastructure | Education (K-12) |
| Developer Tools | Non-profit |
| Fintech | - |
| MarTech | - |
| SalesTech | - |

### Compliance Notes
- CAN-SPAM compliant: all emails must include a valid physical mailing address and a functional one-click unsubscribe mechanism
- Email-validated valid-only contacts from list 1002040 — no unvalidated or catch-all addresses
- No pricing information in any email communication
- Only approved quantitative claim is '750M+ contacts' — no other statistics or proof points not grounded in provided context
- Landing page link must be hosted on the sending domain — never graph8.com — to protect deliverability
- Step 1 must be linkless to maintain inbox placement and avoid spam filter triggers
- Claude Team/Enterprise recipients may require workspace admin enablement — do not overstate ease of setup for this segment
- Do not reference competitor products by name in email copy
- All sends must originate from warmed sending infrastructure on the campaign's designated sending domain

---

## Strategic Rationale

## Strategic Narrative

This campaign targets one of the most underserved and time-pressured segments in modern B2B sales: the full-cycle Account Executive at a sub-5,000-employee tech or software company. These reps carry quota without the organizational backstop of SDRs, RevOps analysts, or dedicated research teams. Every hour spent rebuilding a territory list, hunting down a missing stakeholder's mobile number, or triangulating org charts before an enterprise discovery call is an hour not spent closing. The graph8 MCP server directly attacks this hidden productivity tax — not by adding another app to the stack, but by embedding 750M+ verified B2B contact records into the conversational AI workflow these sellers are already using. For Claude users, setup is a single paste of a custom connector; for everyone else, the graph8 browser platform offers 2,500 free credits at signup. The conversion event is not a meeting — it is a moment of immediate, irreversible value realization.

The two-step email sequence is engineered to match how skeptical, time-starved sellers actually read cold email. Step 1 names the pain precisely — the full-cycle pinch where sourcing time competes with closing time — and asks for nothing more than a reply. No links, no friction, no reason to distrust. Step 2 earns the click by delivering something tangible before the ask: a paste-ready territory research or committee-mapping prompt the seller can use immediately, paired with a single link to a sending-domain landing page that demonstrates the product in action. This architecture respects the inbox, protects deliverability, and aligns the content with the mental model of a seller who evaluates tools by whether they save time in the next ten minutes. Trigger signals — new territory assignments, company hiring surges, active Claude usage, and post-funding growth pressure — are chosen because they mark the exact moments when research overhead becomes acutely felt rather than chronically tolerated.

The channel-and-offer combination is deliberately self-serve and bottoms-up. There is no sales call to book, no demo to schedule, no procurement cycle to survive. The goal is to get a full-cycle AE from cold email to working MCP connector or active platform account within a single session — and to let the product's immediate utility do the retention work. This PLG motion is strategically appropriate for the audience: individual contributors make their own tool decisions at companies under 5,000 employees, and they adopt tools that prove value before asking for commitment. By anchoring the entire sequence to a conversion event (setup or signup) rather than a meeting, the campaign measures the one outcome that actually predicts long-term product adoption, and avoids the pipeline-inflation trap of counting meetings that never convert.

# Messaging & Objections: PLG MCP · Tech & Software · AE

## Angles

### angle_1: Efficiency Play — Double Cost of Pipeline
**Hook:** Full cycle sellers pay for pipeline twice — 750M+ contacts inside Claude turn territory research into a question.
**Pain Point:** Account Executives running full-cycle carry the burden of both sourcing and closing — burning hours on territory research, list building, and contact discovery before a single conversation starts. That's pipeline cost doubled before quota even begins.
**Value Prop:** graph8's autonomous revenue platform gives full-cycle AEs direct access to 750M+ contacts through a natural-language MCP layer inside Claude, collapsing territory research from days to seconds and letting sellers stay in selling motion.
**Best For:** Full-cycle AEs and player-coach sales leaders in Tech & Software companies where reps own prospecting through close

### angle_2: Pain Agitation — The Hidden Tax on Full-Cycle Sellers
**Hook:** Every hour your AE spends building lists is an hour they're not closing — and most teams never measure that tax.
**Pain Point:** Tech and software sales orgs that rely on full-cycle AEs absorb a hidden productivity drag: reps context-switch between research tools, CRMs, and spreadsheets to build pipeline they were hired to close. The cost is invisible until quota miss becomes a pattern.
**Value Prop:** graph8 replaces the research-and-assemble workflow with an AI-native pipeline layer — autonomous agents handle prospecting, contact enrichment, and territory mapping so AEs reclaim selling hours and leadership finally sees the real cost of status quo eliminated.
**Best For:** Revenue leaders and sales ops stakeholders at Tech & Software firms experiencing AE productivity plateaus or missed pipeline targets

### angle_3: Trigger-Based — Scaling Without Adding Headcount
**Hook:** Just expanded your AE team? The last thing you need is each new rep spending their first 90 days building a territory from scratch.
**Pain Point:** When Tech & Software companies grow or restructure their sales teams — through hiring surges, territory realignment, or post-funding expansion — every AE restart on research compounds ramp time and delays revenue contribution.
**Value Prop:** graph8's autonomous revenue platform gives new and existing AEs instant territory coverage through 750M+ contacts queryable in plain language inside Claude — so ramp looks like a question, not a quarter.
**Best For:** VP Sales and CROs at recently funded or rapidly hiring Tech & Software companies realigning territories or onboarding AE cohorts

### angle_4: Authority/Insight — AI-Native Selling Is Already Here
**Hook:** The AEs closing at the top of the leaderboard aren't working harder — they've stopped paying for pipeline twice.
**Pain Point:** Sales organizations in Tech & Software that haven't restructured around AI-native workflows are watching their best reps spend 30–50% of their time on non-selling activity. That's not a rep problem — it's a tooling problem.
**Value Prop:** graph8 is purpose-built for this shift: an autonomous revenue platform that embeds AI agents directly into deal execution, forecasting, and pipeline generation — replacing the legacy CRM-plus-enrichment-plus-sequencing stack with a single intelligent layer.
**Best For:** Forward-thinking CROs, RevOps leaders, and AE managers in Tech & Software who are actively evaluating how AI changes the sales motion

### angle_5: Social Proof — Revenue Teams Moving to Autonomous Pipeline
**Hook:** Revenue teams replacing traditional CRM and manual prospecting with graph8's autonomous agents are reclaiming the hours that were quietly killing quota attainment.
**Pain Point:** Full-cycle AEs in Tech & Software are caught between bloated tool stacks — CRM, enrichment, sequencing, quoting — all requiring manual input that compounds into lost selling time every single week.
**Value Prop:** graph8 consolidates pipeline management, forecasting, deal operations, and contact discovery into one autonomous platform — the same system purpose-built to replace traditional CRM and quoting tools for revenue leaders who need results, not more dashboards.
**Best For:** Sales leaders evaluating CRM replacement or stack consolidation, and AEs frustrated with stitching together disconnected tools to hit number

---

## Approved Proof & Claims

### Allowed Claims
- graph8 provides access to 750M+ contacts queryable through natural language inside Claude via MCP integration (graph8 platform capability)
- graph8 is an autonomous revenue platform that replaces traditional CRM, quoting, and deal operations for revenue leaders (graph8 company description)
- graph8 combines AI agents with sales execution to manage pipeline, forecasting, and deal operations in a single platform (graph8 company description)
- Full-cycle AEs pay for pipeline twice — absorbing both prospecting cost and closing cost — making territory research automation a direct quota lever (graph8 primary campaign hook)
- graph8's autonomous agents are purpose-built to replace the legacy CRM-plus-enrichment-plus-sequencing stack for Tech & Software sales teams (graph8 platform positioning)

### Proof Points

| Type | Content | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| statistic | Full-cycle AEs carry a dual cost burden — sourcing AND closing — meaning every hour spent on territory research and list building is pipeline budget spent before a single selling conversation begins. | graph8 campaign positioning, PLG MCP · Tech & Software · AE |
| social_proof | graph8's autonomous revenue platform is trusted by revenue leaders to replace traditional CRM, quoting, and deal operations — consolidating the full sales execution stack into one AI-native layer. | graph8 company profile and platform description |
| case_study | Revenue teams using graph8's MCP integration can turn territory research into a natural-language question inside Claude — accessing 750M+ contacts without switching tools, building lists, or leaving their AI workflow. | graph8 platform capability, MCP contact layer |

### Banned Phrases
- Best in class (unsubstantiated superlative)
- Revolutionary (overused, no proof)
- Guaranteed results (legal/compliance risk)
- We're the only solution (likely false and unverifiable)
- Industry-leading (requires third-party validation not on file)
- Game-changer (vague, non-specific)
- Disruptive (overused in Tech & Software context, adds no value)
- End-to-end solution (generic, meaningless to AE buyer)
- Seamless integration (unverified without technical proof)
- AI-powered (too generic — use 'autonomous agents' or 'AI-native' with specificity)

---

## Personalization Policy

### Allowed Signals (use freely)
- Company name and industry vertical (Tech & Software)
- Prospect job title and sales function (AE, VP Sales, CRO, RevOps)
- Company size and approximate team structure (inferred from public data)
- Recent public funding announcements
- Job postings indicating AE hiring or territory expansion
- Current tech stack signals from public job descriptions (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach)
- LinkedIn public profile — title, tenure, career history

### Gated Signals (use with high confidence only)
- Hiring volume or AE headcount growth (use only if confirmed via public job boards with recency)
- Revenue estimates (only if publicly reported or from verified sources)
- Specific CRM or sales tool usage (only reference if high-confidence from job postings or public data)
- Territory restructuring or reorg signals (only if confirmed via press or public announcements)

### Forbidden Signals
- Personal social media content (non-professional platforms)
- Health, family, or personal life information
- Salary, compensation, or OTE data
- Non-public or confidential company financials
- Inferred political or religious affiliations
- Any data sourced from non-public or scraped personal profiles

---

# Targeting & Routing: PLG MCP · Tech & Software · AE

## ICP Slice
**Primary ICP:** Account Executive or AE-adjacent revenue leader at a 50–500 employee software or technology company actively scaling their sales motion and seeking to replace or augment traditional CRM and pipeline tooling with autonomous AI-driven revenue operations.
**Secondary ICP:** Revenue Operations or Sales Operations leader at a mid-market SaaS company experiencing pipeline visibility or forecasting challenges who could champion an autonomous revenue platform evaluation.

### Inclusion Criteria
- Company size: 51-500
- Revenue: 5 Million to 100 Million
- Industry: Software Development, Technology, Information and Internet, Information Technology and Services, Artificial Intelligence, Apps, Software, IT System Custom Software Development, Business Intelligence Platforms, Data Infrastructure and Analytics, Computer and Network Security, Internet Marketplace Platforms
- Geography: United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia
- Tech stack: Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Salesloft, Gong, Apollo, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator

### Exclusion Criteria
- Salesforce
- HubSpot
- Microsoft Dynamics
- Pipedrive
- Zoho CRM
- Monday.com CRM
- Clari
- Chorus.ai
- People.ai
- Existing customers
- Government Administration
- Non-profit Organizations
- Primary and Secondary Education
- Higher Education
- Hospitals and Health Care
- Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
- Companies with fewer than 10 employees
- Companies with no dedicated sales team or AE function
- Companies currently in bankruptcy or wind-down
- Staffing and recruiting firms without product-led growth motion

## Allowed Titles & Personas

|---------|--------|-----------|----------|
| Account Executive (AE) | Account Executive, Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Account Executive, Mid-Market Account Executive, Strategic Account Executive, Sales Executive, Field Sales Executive | Senior | P1 |
| VP / Head of Sales | VP of Sales, Vice President of Sales, Head of Sales, VP Revenue, Chief Revenue Officer, CRO, SVP Sales | Vice President | P1 |
| Revenue / Sales Operations | Director of Revenue Operations, Head of Sales Operations, Revenue Operations Manager, Sales Operations Lead, VP of Revenue Operations, Director of Sales Operations | Director | P2 |
| Founder / CEO (SMB) | Founder, Co-Founder, CEO, Chief Executive Officer, Managing Director, President | CXO | P2 |

## Scoring & Prioritization
### Fit Score (0-100)
- Company size match: 25
- Industry match: 30
- Tech stack match: 20
- Title match: 25

### Intent Signals
- Actively hiring Account Executives or Sales Development Representatives: +25 (Scaling the sales headcount signals investment in outbound pipeline growth — a direct use case for graph8's autonomous revenue platform and AE productivity tooling.)
- Job postings for RevOps, Sales Ops, or CRM Administrator roles: +20 (Hiring for revenue operations or CRM administration indicates the company is actively managing or overhauling their sales stack, making them receptive to a CRM replacement or augmentation pitch.)
- Recent Series A, B, or C funding announcement: +20 (Post-funding companies face pressure to accelerate pipeline and forecasting accuracy, creating urgency around autonomous revenue operations tools.)
- LinkedIn activity or content around sales productivity, pipeline management, or AI in sales: +15 (Engagement with topics directly related to graph8's value proposition indicates the prospect is already researching or experiencing pain in this area.)
- G2 or Capterra review activity on CRM or sales engagement tools: +15 (Reviewing or comparing CRM and sales engagement software signals active evaluation — a prime window for graph8 outreach.)
- Tech stack includes legacy CRM (Salesforce or HubSpot) alongside point solutions (Gong, Outreach, Apollo): +10 (A fragmented sales stack with multiple point solutions is the core pain graph8 solves — consolidating pipeline, forecasting, and deal execution into one autonomous platform.)

### Trigger Events
- New VP of Sales or CRO hired within the last 90 days: Launch high-touch sequence immediately — new sales leaders typically audit and replace tooling within their first 90 days; prioritize meeting CTA with executive-level angle.
- Company announces new funding round (Series A–C): Enroll in high-touch sequence with ROI-focused angle emphasizing pipeline acceleration and forecasting accuracy to support growth mandate from investors.
- Company posts 3+ open AE or SDR roles simultaneously: Trigger standard sequence targeting VP Sales and RevOps personas with messaging around scaling outbound without proportional headcount increases.
- Prospect engages with graph8 content (email open 3+, website visit, LinkedIn interaction): Move to high-touch sequence and fast-track to meeting CTA; notify assigned AE for personalized follow-up within 24 hours.
- CRM contract renewal window detected (6–12 months out from Salesforce or HubSpot renewal): Enroll in standard sequence with displacement/replacement angle and ROI comparison content; target both economic buyer and RevOps champion simultaneously.

## DNC Rules
- **Hard DNC:** Contacts who have submitted a formal opt-out or unsubscribe request, Contacts flagged with legal cease-and-desist, Existing graph8 customers (all tiers), Known competitor employees (Salesforce, HubSpot, Clari, People.ai, Chorus.ai, Microsoft Dynamics), Contacts at companies currently in active legal dispute with graph8
- **Soft DNC:** Prospects contacted within the last 30 days with no engagement — hold for 30-day cooling period, Contacts who replied with 'not interested' in the last 90 days — re-evaluate at 90-day mark, Out-of-office auto-reply detected — pause sequence for 5 business days, Prospects in active deal stage (SQLs or opportunities) — route to AE, remove from automated sequences, Contacts at companies that recently completed a CRM implementation (within 6 months)
- **Channel-specific:** No cold calls to C-suite (CXO/CRO) without prior email engagement or warm introduction, LinkedIn InMail limited to P1 personas only (AE and VP Sales) — do not send InMail to P3 contacts, No SMS outreach for this campaign — email only per campaign channel designation, Maximum 1 follow-up email per 5 business days per contact to avoid spam classification

### Must Follow
- Use ONLY the approved number: 750M+ contacts. No other statistics or proof points unless explicitly listed in campaign_context.proof_points

### Must Never Do
- Never use em dashes (--) in subject lines or body copy. Use commas, periods, semicolons, or hyphens instead.

- Never mention pricing
- Never link to graph8.com

- Never use forbidden personalization signals: personal social media, salary, family info, health-related data, political affiliation

### Format Rules
- Subject lines: 5-8 words, all lowercase, reference a trigger signal when available
- Opening line: one sentence, specific to the contact or account signal
- Body flow: Problem they face → How graph8 solves it → Single approved proof point (if available) → CTA
- No paragraph longer than 2 sentences
- CTA is the final line before sign-off
- Email 1 (step_001): no links
- Email 2 (step_002): one link to sending-domain landing page only

## Do Not Send Conditions
- **target.email or target.first_name is missing:** Cannot personalize or deliver safely - required fields absent
- **target.dnc_flag === true:** Compliance violation - contact is on the Do Not Contact list
- **target.bounced_email === true:** Email previously bounced - sending would harm sender reputation
- **target.title_score < 0.5:** Contact title is outside the target persona (AE / full-cycle seller at US tech/software company under 5,000 employees)
- **target.recent_negative_reply === true:** Contact has replied negatively or opted out - must respect the no
- **target.touches_this_week >= 3:** Contact policy limit reached - do not exceed 3 touches per week
- **Company headcount exceeds 5,000 employees:** Out of target segment - campaign targets companies under 5,000 employees

## Style Guidelines
- **Subject lines:** 5-8 words, all lowercase, no spam triggers, reference a specific trigger signal (hiring activity, funding, news). Pattern-interrupt without being clickbait.
- **Opening line:** One sentence. Reference something specific and observable about the contact or their company (signal-led). No generic openers like 'Companies like yours...' or 'Hope this finds you well'.
- **Body - Value Bridge:** Follow the Problem → Solution → Proof flow. Lead with the full-cycle seller pain (sourcing time competing with closing time). Bridge to graph8 MCP server: 750M+ B2B contacts searchable from Claude chat. One proof point maximum if available.
- **CTA:** Email 1: soft_ask only - a single, low-friction question that invites a reply. Email 2: content CTA with one sending-domain link. Email 3: direct calendar/meeting request. No aggressive asks before trust is established.
- **Tone:** Professional and direct, but human. No buzzwords, no jargon. Write the way a thoughtful senior AE would write to a peer. Short sentences. Active voice.
- **Closing:** Sign off with sender name only. No 'Best regards,' templates. Keep it minimal.
- **Em dashes:** Never use em dashes (--). Use commas, periods, semicolons, or hyphens (-) instead. Em dashes are an AI/spam detection signal.

## Response Time Guidelines

**Positive Interest:** Respond within 1 hour. Buying intent decays fast — a delayed response to a "yes" is a lost meeting. If you can't respond personally, send the calendar link immediately via automation and follow up with a personal note.

**Soft Interest:** Respond within 4 hours. They're evaluating — a prompt, thoughtful reply with a relevant resource signals professionalism and builds credibility before they move on.

**Objection:** Respond within 2 hours. Objections are buying signals in disguise. A fast, measured response shows confidence and keeps the conversation from going cold. Don't over-craft — a direct reply beats a perfect one sent tomorrow.

**Referral:** Respond within 1 hour. Warm intros have a short half-life. Reach out to the referred contact the same day and always reference the referrer by name in your opening line.

**Not Now:** Respond within 4 hours. Acknowledge timing gracefully, lock in a specific follow-up date, and get out of their inbox. Dragging it out loses the goodwill.

**Negative / DNC:** Respond within 24 hours with a graceful exit. If a DNC has been explicitly requested, action the suppression immediately — do not wait. No response is acceptable only if they've asked to be left alone entirely.

**Out of Office:** No response needed. Action the sequence pause within the same business day. Set the resume task for 1 business day after their stated return date.

---

## Escalation Rules

- Tier 1 account (as defined in CRM) shows any positive interest — notify the assigned AE within 1 hour and loop them into the reply thread before sending.
- Enterprise deal potential (100+ seat org, VP or above title, multi-team use case mentioned) — escalate to AE immediately, do not attempt to close the meeting solo.
- Complex technical questions about data sourcing, Claude integration, API access, or compliance — escalate to AE or Solutions Engineer; do not guess or improvise an answer.
- Pricing authority is required (prospect asks for custom pricing, volume discounts, or enterprise contracts) — do not quote; escalate to AE or hand off to a pricing conversation.
- Legal or compliance concerns raised (data privacy, GDPR, SOC 2, contractual requirements) — escalate to AE and loop in legal/compliance team before responding.
- Prospect is a known competitive account or named strategic target — flag to manager before any follow-up so outreach can be coordinated at the account level.
- Inbound referral comes from a C-suite contact or board-level connection — treat as Tier 1 and escalate to AE regardless of company size or deal stage.

## Usage Guidelines

- **Check freshness before every send:** Statistics, case study metrics, and social proof numbers have expiration dates. Verify that any statistic used is from research published within the last 18 months and that customer results referenced are still accurate and approved. Outdated proof points erode credibility fast — especially with technical and ops-savvy buyers in Tech & Software.
- **Match snippets to persona and seniority:** Not every snippet works for every contact. Use strategic, outcome-focused language (forecast accuracy, revenue predictability) for VP and C-level buyers. Use tactical, day-to-day language (less CRM admin, more selling time) for AE and IC-level contacts. Mismatched messaging signals that you don't understand your buyer's world.
- **Don't stack proof points:** One sharp, specific, relevant proof point will always outperform three generic ones. If you're tempted to include a case study, a stat, and a logo reference in the same message — stop. Pick the single strongest one for that persona and let it land. Stacking proof reads as desperation and dilutes the impact of each individual point.
- **Customize every bracket before sending:** Every [bracketed placeholder] in these snippets must be replaced with a real, verified, specific value before the message goes out. A visible bracket in a sent email is a trust-killer. Build a habit of doing a final bracket-check as the last step before hitting send or enrolling in a sequence.
- **Lead with relevance, not product:** Snippets are most effective when they follow a relevant, personalized opener — not when they lead. Use personalization snippets first to establish context and signal genuine research, then layer in proof or CTA snippets. Dropping a proof point cold, without context, reads as copy-paste and gets ignored.
- **Use one CTA per message — and make it clear:** Each outreach message should contain exactly one call to action. Mixing a soft ask with a meeting request with a content offer creates confusion and reduces reply rates. Choose the CTA that best matches where the prospect is in the buying journey and commit to it.
